page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU features a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_ni. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the c3d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the average range. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 565.97 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, measuring 37.36 GB/sec and 14.86 GB/sec respectively.

The instance is applicable for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, Redis operations, and basic text or image processing, where it delivers average throughput. However, it exhibits poor performance for medium-sized language model inference, with text generation on a 7B model dropping to 5.95 tokens/sec. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs, combined with weak uncached memory bandwidth, represents a tradeoff for data-intensive or memory-bound analytics.
